hypothesis: Directed networks in which every node is of one type and has exactly two outgoing connections can realize, through the connection pattern alone, structures equivalent to d-dimensional arrays for every d, as well as trees and nested (fractal) structures. 'Equivalent to a d-dimensional array' is taken in Wolfram's two senses: (i) grouping nodes into identical blocks yields exactly the d-dimensional grid (each block connected to its 2d neighbouring blocks), and (ii) the number of nodes reachable within r connection steps grows like r^d (the network dimension criterion of NKS chapter 9).
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. (1) Arrays: for d = 1..6 construct the network by one uniform rule: each lattice point x of Z^d is a block of d nodes (x, i), i = 0..d-1, and node (x, i) has exactly two outgoing connections, to (x + e_i, (i+1) mod d) and (x - e_i, (i+1) mod d). Verify (a) every node has out-degree exactly 2 and the rule is identical for every node; (b) exact structural equivalence: on the torus (Z_L)^d with L = 5, contracting each block to a point gives a multigraph whose edge set equals the d-dimensional grid's edge set {x <-> x +- e_i} with every block connected to exactly 2d distinct neighbouring blocks (exact set comparison); (c) dimension criterion: breadth-first search along connections from one node of the infinite network, counting N(r) = nodes within r steps; the growth exponent log2(N(R)/N(R/2)) at R = 20 d must lie within 0.5 of d for d = 1, 2, 3, 4 (so that it rounds to d), and is reported (not scored) for d = 5, 6. (2) Trees: the infinite binary tree (node k connects to 2k+1 and 2k+2) has N(r) = 2^(r+1) - 1 for r <= 15 (exact). (3) Nested: the level-7 Sierpinski gasket graph (3 corner nodes of degree 2, all others of degree 4) is given an Eulerian orientation along an Euler circuit plus a directed 3-cycle through the corners, which must give every node out-degree exactly 2; its undirected growth exponent log2(N(R)/N(R/2)) at R = 64 from a corner must lie within 0.3 of log2(3) = 1.585, the gasket's dimension. 'Supports' if (1a), (1b), (1c), (2) and (3) all hold.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' if the uniform construction fails structurally for some d <= 6 (out-degree not 2, or the block quotient is not the d-dimensional grid), or if the measured growth exponent for some d <= 4 rounds to an integer other than d, or if no out-degree-2 orientation of the gasket exists. 'Mixed' if arrays pass but the tree or nested construction fails its criterion. 'Inconclusive' is not expected: the test is a self-contained computation.
interpretation: The claim is constructive and existential: one explicit family of networks suffices for each d, plus one tree and one nested example. The block-quotient check is the exact sense of 'equivalent to an array'; the growth exponent is Wolfram's own operational notion of network dimension (NKS p. 479 and notes) and adds a check that the effective geometry is d-dimensional without reference to the blocks. Blocks of d nodes connected to 2d neighbouring blocks follow the description on NKS p. 195 ('every block of nodes is connected to four rather than two neighboring blocks'). Growth exponents at finite radius are biased low (the lattice ball itself has local exponent below d at radius ~20), hence the +-0.5 window; the exact quotient check is the decisive part.

generator.program_family: d-dimensional block networks (blocks of d nodes, node (x,i) -> (x+e_i,(i+1) mod d) and (x-e_i,(i+1) mod d)) for d = 1..6; infinite binary tree; level-7 Sierpinski gasket with an Eulerian orientation
generator.initial_conditions: BFS from node (0,0) of the infinite block network, from the root of the tree, from a corner of the gasket
generator.steps: BFS radius R = 20 d (arrays), 15 (tree), 64 (gasket); torus side L = 5 for the quotient check

datasets.name: NKS pp. 195-196, 'Network Systems' (online edition)
datasets.role: source of the block description used for the construction
